name: Sulwhasoo

card.summary: A Korean luxury skincare brand from Amorepacific that pairs traditional herbal ingredients with modern skincare science to improve skin look and feel.
card.note: Premium-priced cosmetic line; individual products vary in ingredients, so check labels for allergens.

quick.overview:
Sulwhasoo is a skincare and cosmetics brand launched by South Korea's Amorepacific in 1997. It combines traditional Korean herbal ingredients with modern skincare science, aimed at a smoother, more radiant and healthier-looking complexion.

The name refers to a plum blossom that blooms in the snow. The line is sold across Asia, North America, Europe and Australia, and has featured celebrity ambassadors including Song Hye-kyo, Rose and Tilda Swinton.
quick.how: Used as a conventional skincare routine of cleansers, toners, serums, creams and masks applied topically; products vary by line, and a flagship cream is marketed under the Jaum name. Visible results from cosmetics generally build with regular use.
quick.risks: As cosmetics, products can cause irritation or allergy in sensitive people, particularly with botanical extracts and fragrance. Ingredients differ across the range.

lead: Sulwhasoo is a skincare and cosmetics brand introduced by Amorepacific Corporation in 1997.[1] It is marketed as combining Korean traditional herbal ingredients with modern skincare science.[1]

The name refers to a plum blossom that blooms in the snow.[1] Amorepacific, which traces its roots to a 1930s camellia-oil business and was founded as Pacific Chemical in 1945, owns more than 30 brands including Laneige, Innisfree and Mamonde alongside Sulwhasoo.[2]
Brand ambassadors have included Song Hye-kyo (2018), Angelababy (2019), Taeyeon (2021), Rose (2022), Tilda Swinton (2023), Choi Hwa-jung (2024) and Im Yoon-ah (2025).[1]

chain: Herbal-based creams and serums applied daily
angle.text: Sulwhasoo products are used as a moisturising and anti-ageing routine to improve how the skin looks, through hydration and conditioning ingredients rather than medical treatment.

paras: Amorepacific launched Sulwhasoo in 1997 and positions it around traditional Korean herbal ingredients plus modern science.[1] A flagship cream is promoted under the Jaum name.[1]

Amorepacific began in the 1930s when Madame Dokjeong Yun sold camellia oil in Kaesong; her son Sungwhan Suh took over in 1945 and built the business as Pacific Chemical, and the company took the Amorepacific name in 2002.[2]
The brand uses high-profile ambassadors, listed from 2018 to 2025 across Korean, Chinese and international celebrities.[1]
